name: Sao Tome and Principe
tagline: Two volcanic islands and a lot of cocoa
summary: Obo rainforest running from the peaks to the sea, volcanic plugs standing out of the forest, abandoned cocoa plantations being taken back by it, and some of the best chocolate in the world made where the beans grow.
when: The gravana, June to September, is the dry season. December and January are a shorter one.

entries.caption: Pico Cao Grande
entries.description: A volcanic plug standing three hundred metres straight out of the rainforest.
entries.subject: the needle of Pico Cao Grande rising from rainforest

entries.caption: Obo
entries.description: Rainforest covering a third of Sao Tome, from the peaks down to the shore.
entries.subject: dense Obo rainforest running down to the sea

entries.caption: Endemic Birds
entries.description: Twenty-eight species live on these islands and nowhere else — one of the highest rates on earth.
entries.subject: a Sao Tome giant weaver on a branch in Obo forest

entries.caption: Sea, Not Savanna
entries.description: There are no large mammals. What there is instead is birds, turtles and whales.
entries.subject: a humpback whale off the coast of Principe

entries.caption: Pico de Sao Tome
entries.description: 2,024 metres, in cloud most of the year, and a two-day walk to the top.
entries.subject: the cloud-covered summit of Pico de Sao Tome above forest

entries.caption: Sao Nicolau
entries.description: A waterfall in the forest above Trindade, reached on a short walk from the road.
entries.subject: the Sao Nicolau waterfall falling through dense forest

entries.caption: Rivers to the Sea
entries.description: Short, steep rivers off the volcanic interior, and pools in most of them.
entries.subject: a clear river running over volcanic rock through forest

entries.caption: Praia Jale and Banana Beach
entries.description: Turtle-nesting sand in the south of Sao Tome, and the curved bay on Principe.
entries.subject: the curved palm-backed sand of Banana Beach on Principe

entries.caption: The Cocoa Forest
entries.description: Plantations abandoned in the 1970s and taken back by the forest, with the trees still fruiting.
entries.subject: cocoa pods growing among overgrown plantation trees

entries.caption: Walking and Diving
entries.description: Cao Grande and the Pico on foot, and volcanic reef straight off the beaches.
entries.subject: walkers on a forest trail below Pico Cao Grande

entries.caption: Creole, and Portuguese
entries.description: Forro, Angolar and Principense creoles, and a culture built on the plantations and against them.
entries.subject: a street of Portuguese colonial buildings in Sao Tome town

entries.caption: The Angolares
entries.description: Descended from a shipwreck or a maroon community, depending on who tells it, and fishermen either way.
entries.subject: Angolares fishermen with a dugout canoe on a black beach

entries.caption: Calulu and Chocolate
entries.description: Calulu — fish stewed with okra and palm oil — and chocolate made where the beans grow.
entries.subject: a plate of calulu with breadfruit and rice

entries.caption: Auto de Floripes
entries.description: A Principe street play that runs a whole day in August, performed since the sixteenth century.
entries.subject: costumed performers in the Auto de Floripes on Principe

entries.caption: Cocoa, Coffee and Carving
entries.description: Single-origin chocolate, island coffee, and carving in the plantation villages.
entries.subject: cocoa beans drying on a wooden rack in the sun

entries.caption: The Rocas
entries.description: Plantation estates with hospitals, chapels and rail lines, most of them now half-ruined and lived in.
entries.subject: the arcaded courtyard of an abandoned roca plantation house

entries.caption: Principe Biosphere
entries.description: The whole of Principe is a UNESCO biosphere reserve, and it is seven thousand people.
entries.subject: forested peaks and coastline on Principe island

entries.caption: Sao Tome Town
entries.description: A small Portuguese colonial capital with a fort, a market and a cathedral.
entries.subject: the pastel colonial buildings and fort at Sao Tome town

entries.caption: Portuguese Colonial and Roca
entries.description: Pastel colonial in town, and the plantation architecture of the rocas in the interior.
entries.subject: the tower and arcades of Roca Agostinho Neto

entries.caption: The Fish Landing
entries.description: Dugouts come in through the surf and the fish is sold on the sand within the hour.
entries.subject: fishermen landing dugout canoes through surf on a black beach

entries.caption: Small and Easy
entries.description: Short distances, calm bays and no dangerous animals — one of the easier African countries with children.
entries.subject: children swimming in a calm bay on Sao Tome

entries.caption: Climbing the Pico
entries.description: Two days through cloud forest, with a night in a shelter and a lot of rain.
entries.subject: a muddy trail through mossy cloud forest on the Pico

entries.caption: Good, and Small
entries.description: Restored rocas turned into hotels, and a serious eco-resort on Principe.
entries.subject: a restored plantation house hotel with a verandah

entries.caption: Cocoa, Grown and Made
entries.description: Cooperatives grow it, and the chocolate is made on the island rather than shipped raw.
entries.subject: a chocolate maker sorting cocoa beans on a table

entries.caption: Volcano and Canopy
entries.description: Cao Grande through cloud in the early morning, from the road below it.
entries.subject: cloud parting around Pico Cao Grande above forest at dawn

entries.caption: Roca Agostinho Neto
entries.description: The largest plantation on the island, ruined, lived in, and quite unlike anywhere else.
entries.subject: families living in the arcaded ruins of a roca plantation

entries.caption: Why Sao Tome and Principe
entries.description: Rainforest to the shore, twenty-eight endemic birds, and chocolate made where it grows.
entries.subject: a volcanic peak above rainforest and an empty beach
